title: Reduce complexity
why: A function exceeds configured complexity thresholds.
suggestion: Split or simplify the function, or document a local suppression when one cohesive parser or traversal must retain shared state.
limitations: JavaScript and TypeScript extraction covers named declarations, methods, and block-bodied variable arrow functions.
JavaScript and TypeScript anonymous callbacks and expression-bodied arrow functions are not measured; executable Rust closure branches remain charged to their enclosing named function.
Cyclomatic complexity counts each logical operator. Cognitive complexity counts a consecutive chain of the same logical operator once; Rust chains span line breaks and reset at expression boundaries.
Complex localization implementations are grouped into one repository finding with related locations.
Python comments and single-line or triple-quoted string contents are excluded from complexity signals.
Rust complexity measurement excludes nested named callable bodies and local impl declarations from their enclosing function without changing extracted sources or locations.
Recognized empty Rust closure delimiters are not boolean OR operators; executable branches inside closures, async blocks and ordinary runtime macros remain measured.

Rust quote!/quote_spanned! and syn parse_quote!/parse_quote_spanned! templates are excluded for direct qualified calls or explicit direct/grouped imports, including simple aliases. Evaluated span expressions remain measured; lexical macro_rules shadowing and block-scoped imports are respected conservatively.

Single-arm local macro_rules wrappers can exclude one token-tree capture forwarded exactly once directly to a proven unspanned quote macro. Bounded identifier/token-tree matchers and terminal identifier-list repetitions are supported; other arguments remain measured. Explicit sibling imports and aliases require conventional, unambiguous module declarations and an explicit provider re-export.

Custom wrappers with runtime reuse of the quoted capture, branching setup, nested macro invocations, multiple arms, unsupported fragments, spanned forwarding or more than 32 token-tree nesting levels remain measured. Wildcards, path-mapped modules, transitive re-exports, qualified custom-wrapper calls and unresolved macro names are not expanded; full Rust name resolution is not performed.

Rust match contributes one nested cognitive control and arms minus one cyclomatic alternatives; guards and executable arm bodies remain measured, without treating pattern, struct or arm braces as extra control nesting.

Rust functions consisting solely of one unguarded match that maps simple patterns to literals, conventionally uppercase constant paths or borrowed literal arrays do not receive refactoring advice; their cyclomatic and cognitive metrics are unchanged. Guards, calls, nested matches, executable blocks and surrounding statements remain advisory candidates. Unsupported literal and pattern syntax is retained conservatively.

Rust nesting follows recognized control, closure and async bodies rather than arbitrary braces. Callable boundaries and pending control headers are lexical; unsupported inline declarations, complex nested header expressions and unresolved macro syntax can remain approximate.
